findings.title: Backup-code login can skip the password check by sending a dummy totpCode
findings.body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` branch runs before any TOTP validation and never looks at `totpCode`. A request with `email`, a bogus non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") and a valid `backupCode` skips password verification and then authenticates on the backup code alone. Before this PR a bogus `totpCode` failed the TOTP check. Now it does not, because the backup branch short-circuits it. Backup codes are static, long-lived secrets, so this makes them a standalone credential that replaces the password. The backup branch should verify the password itself, or the password skip should be conditioned on a TOTP code that is actually validated.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The codes are decrypted, the matching entry is set to null, and the whole array is re-encrypted and written back, with no transaction or compare-and-set. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both read it as unused and both succeed, so 'usable exactly once' is not guaranteed. Concurrent consumption of two different codes can also overwrite each other. The second write restores the code the first request just burned. An atomic update guarded on the previous ciphertext value, or a transaction with row locking, would fix this.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable/resetState
findings.body: After a successful enable, the modal moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` and hides the Cancel button. The dialog is still dismissable through `onOpenChange` (Escape or clicking the overlay). That path calls neither `onEnable()` nor `resetState()`. The parent is not told 2FA is now enabled, so the settings switch can stay stale until a reload. When the modal is reopened the component may still be on the backup-codes step with the old codes. Backup codes cannot be shown again, so a user who dismisses by accident can lose them. The close handler should route through the same cleanup as the Close button, or the dialog should not be dismissable on this step.

findings.title: Backup codes and blob URL are never cleared or revoked when the modal closes
findings.body: `resetState` only resets the password, error message and step. The plaintext `backupCodes`, `secret` and `dataUri` stay in component state, and the Blob object URL created in `handleSetup` is only revoked if setup is run again. It is not revoked on close or unmount. The sensitive codes therefore stay in memory and the blob URL leaks for the life of the page. Clear this state in `resetState` and revoke the URL in cleanup.

findings.title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting clipboard write
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that rejects on permission denial or in non-secure contexts. It is neither awaited nor caught, and the 'Backup codes copied!' toast is shown unconditionally. A user can believe the codes were copied when they were not, and the codes cannot be retrieved again afterwards.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message points to a settings feature that does not exist
findings.body: Users who enabled 2FA before this PR have no `backupCodes`. If they click 'Lost access' on login or in the disable modal, they get 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' This PR adds no UI or endpoint to generate backup codes for an already-enabled account. Codes are only created in `setup.ts` when enabling 2FA. The message sends users to a nonexistent action, and for them backup-code recovery is simply unavailable. The text should be accurate, or a regenerate flow should be added.

findings.title: No tests for the actual backup-code behavior; first e2e test left on backup-code screen
findings.body: The new logic is not covered: login with a backup code, single-use enforcement, wrong or missing codes, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The TODO on line 12 admits this. The 'enable and login' test never closes the new backup-codes dialog, and its `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` assertion is vacuous because it asserts on a Promise (acknowledged by the new FIXME). The security-sensitive server paths in `authorize` and `disable.ts` have no automated coverage.

findings.title: Unrelated change removes the password show/hide toggle from keyboard navigation globally
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the toggle inside the shared `PasswordField` affects every password field in the app. Keyboard and screen-reader users can no longer tab to the show/hide button, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes. Nothing in this feature requires it, so it should be scoped to the places that need it or dropped.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode type can crash the endpoint with a 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string. A non-string JSON value such as a number or object that is truthy throws a TypeError and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 `IncorrectBackupCode`. The endpoint also has no rate limiting for repeated backup-code guesses, unlike the login path, which calls `checkRateLimitAndThrowError`.
